pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered in full and received warmly but with mechanics questions rather than commitment. He engaged on difficulty first — 'I see his workouts and I've never really used kettlebells, but it does not look too easy. Like it looks easy to watch, but I can believe it's not easy to get those right movements' — which the rep matched with his own first-session story. Then he asked how delivery actually works: 'how does it work necessarily that, like, you have an app, we follow him with an app, we have to, like, videos, like, how does it...' The rep deferred it to the accountability segment. Net reaction: 'Yeah, it's interesting. I'm looking forward to have more information, but it's pretty interesting.'

Accepted the what/when/how-much frame without resistance and mapped it onto his own history — he already knows intermittent fasting works for him and has done 48-hour fasts on electrolytes. His question was about deliverable specificity: 'is there a plan that comes with it or it's like these are the steps and we choose what we want and there's accountability, like follow-ups on what we eat'. The rep clarified that there is no six-month meal plan, only an example plan plus principles, and he accepted it: 'Yeah. Makes sense.'

The most engaged of the three — he played the mechanics back to check he had them right: 'big picture, you have three workouts to do this week, and then I'll have to do the workout, log them, video, probably not every workout'. One point of mild resistance, on the text channel specifically: 'I don't see necessarily texting too much, like, often. I don't think it would be something I would need to do. I mean, as long as I'm all accountable.' The rep corrected it directly — 'he wants you to over-communicate... don't be shy on raising the hand' — and the prospect accepted. Worth noting for the rollup that this pillar is the one he asked for by name at the top of the call and the one his cheaper alternative visibly does better, and the gap between weekly check-ins and his colleague's daily unannounced checks was never closed.

anchors.raw: I'm comparing with my colleague's personal trainer, which he's at 600 a month. And it's not necessarily the same as Trevor, but that's my comparison of pricing.
anchors.competitor: Local personal trainer used by the prospect's colleague; name not given
anchors.note: The hardest anchor in the call and the one the rep never repriced against. $600/month against $1,000/month equivalent is not an outrageous gap — it was closeable on specialisation and scope — but the rep answered it by questioning the competitor's kettlebell competence rather than by building the value difference, so the number stood.

anchors.raw: I have a colleague of mine that used to weigh 400 pounds. And now he's about, I think, 14% body fat, like 185. And he's got a personal trainer, like always texting him... I spent a week with my colleague and it's every, Every day contact. It's really almost like, surprise, show me what you're eating. He has no choice. He can't cheat.
anchors.note: This is what makes the $600 anchor immovable. He has not read about the cheaper option working — he travelled with the result for a week and watched it eat. The programme is being asked to beat a 215 lb transformation he witnessed personally, at less than two thirds the price, with more frequent contact. Nothing in the pillar presentation was positioned against it.

anchors.raw: It's not necessarily... I'm a bit surprised. It's pretty much double what I thought it would have been.
anchors.note: He arrived expecting roughly $3,000 for six months. The setter call did not pre-frame price, so the closer absorbed a 2x expectation gap cold at minute thirty-nine. Relevant to the setter process, not only to this rep.

anchors.raw: 6,000 US. Okay. Correct. I mean, Canadian. I'm going to go see what's the Canadian version of it.
anchors.note: The prospect prices in CAD, so the real number he hears is roughly 8,000-8,500 and the rep converted it live and approximately. Every Canadian prospect in this corpus will experience a materially larger number than the US quote, and there is no defined CAD price to give them.

anchors.raw: I'm doing this at the moment, which I think I've never done before, looking for external help like this.
anchors.note: No history of paying for coaching of any kind. There is no established willingness-to-pay to build on, which is why the number read as steep despite a director-level income.

anchors.raw: he gives you a real guarantee on that, that if you want... Achieve the goals, which are adding more, adding at least eight kilos to your baseline kettlebell moves. He will work for you, work with you until you actually do that. And he will work with you for free. Show me another person in this space that, that actually is giving that.
anchors.note: The only supportive anchor deployed, and it was used well — as a risk-reversal against the unknown-provider objection. It did not move him, which suggests his blocker was provider familiarity rather than outcome risk.

unmet_demand.want: A coach who is local and whose results he can see in person — 'I don't know if it would be better having someone more local and someone that I see that there's results'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is remote by design: Zoom onboarding, an app, recorded form checks and text. There is no local presence to offer and no in-person proof he can go and look at. This is the objection he ended the call intending to act on, and it received no response at all.

unmet_demand.want: Daily, unannounced accountability of the kind he watched work — 'surprise, show me what you're eating. He has no choice. He can't cheat. He's there. I feel like that's what I need.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme offers weekly structured check-ins, app-visible workout completion and open text access to Trevor. That is genuinely close, and the rep's 'if you don't do the workout, he's going to be knocking on your door, virtually' gestures at it, but the pull-based text channel is the opposite of what he described needing and he had already said he would not use it much. Nobody bridged the two.

unmet_demand.want: Something to compare against before deciding — 'I want to have a comparative with my colleague', 'I just want to have a second option'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not a product gap so much as an unanswered buying process. He stated a standing personal rule of never committing without sleeping on it, and the offer had no mechanism to occupy the gap other than a Friday call and some emailed videos. Everything that would have made the comparison favourable — specialisation, the guarantee, the graduate-in-six-months philosophy — was delivered verbally and nothing was left in his hands.
None exists. The rep estimated the conversion live and imprecisely, leaving the prospect to go and work out the real number himself after the call.
